(a) **Active Element**: An element that is capable of delivering energy or power to a circuit independently over time (e.g., voltage and current sources).

(b) **Bilateral Element**: An element in which the voltage-current relationship is the same for current flowing in either direction (e.g., resistance, inductance, capacitance).

(c) **Unilateral Element**: An element in which the voltage-current relationship depends on the direction of current flow, meaning the circuit behavior changes if the polarity is reversed (e.g., diode, transistor).

(d) **Passive Element**: An element that only receives, stores, or dissipates energy and cannot generate power independently (e.g., resistor, inductor, capacitor).
proTip: Clearly differentiate between active/passive based on energy generation/dissipation, and bilateral/unilateral based on directional V-I dependency.
